purpose: Hold the pose model constant at YOLO11n-Pose 640x640 across every platform so the numbers describe the device rather than the device-plus-model. Previously Jetson was only ever benchmarked on YOLO11s/11m while RK and reCamera ran YOLO11n, which made the platforms incomparable.

method.jetson: trtexec --useCudaGraph --noDataTransfers --infStreams=N --duration=10 --warmUp=2000, fixed 1x3x640x640, batch=1 per context. Same flags as the existing YOLO11s/11m rows in RESULTS.md.
method.rknn: platforms/rknn/benchmark.py, blank 640 input, --postprocess-backend cpp, same iteration counts as the FP16 baselines (100 on RK3588, 200 on RK3576).
method.note: Per-frame figures are accelerator inference only. They exclude RTSP decode, letterbox, tracking, the temporal MLP and MQTT.
method.hailo: hailortcli benchmark --time-to-run 15, on an idle Hailo-8 (co-resident mcp_face_rec stopped for the run, restarted after). Reports FPS hw_only/streaming and HW latency; accelerator only, same basis as the trtexec and rknn rows.

orin_nano_coresident.note: openclaw-gateway, mcp_warehouse and mcp_face_rec left running, matching the co-existing-capacity basis used for the YOLO11s/11m rows

orin_nx_idle.note: all co-resident containers stopped for the duration, then restarted

orin_nano_idle.note: openclaw-gateway, mcp_warehouse and mcp_face_rec stopped for the run, then restarted and verified healthy

precision_int8_uncalibrated.why_not: Built with trtexec --int8 --fp16 and NO calibrator or calibration cache, so TensorRT assigns arbitrary dynamic ranges. Valid for kernel timing, worthless for detection. build_engine.sh passes only --fp16; a real INT8 path needs a calibrator plus calibration set implemented in this project, and the temporal profile would then have to be re-frozen on INT8 pose output.

jetson.contention_finding: Contention only matters when the co-resident workload uses the accelerator, and when it does it can invert the ranking. Orin NX measured 264.9 FPS FP16 while running its own GPU inference stack - below Orin Nano, the opposite of the two modules' relative capability; with that stack stopped it is 306.2 FPS. Orin Nano measured identically idle and co-resident (270.5 vs 270.7 FPS) because openclaw-gateway, mcp_warehouse and mcp_face_rec never touch the GPU. The same effect made the first INT8 reading on a busy Orin NX come out at 4.55 ms, slower than its own FP16, which would have read as INT8 being a regression on Jetson; idle it is 2.45 ms.

calibration.source: GMDCSA-24, letterboxed to 640x640 exactly as platforms/rknn/video_source.py does (aspect_fit_geometry + pad_scaled_rgb, INTER_LINEAR, pad value 114, centred)
calibration.spread: subjects 1-4, ADL and Fall, 3 evenly spaced frames per clip; the other 240 frames of the extraction were held out for the sanity check

detection_sanity.selection: held out of the calibration set; one Fall and one ADL per subject
detection_sanity.verdict: Identical detection counts on every frame on both boards. Boxes agree within about 1 px, scores within +/-0.04, and visible-keypoint counts match on all high-confidence detections.
caveats: subject-3_Fall_01_1.jpg yields 0 detections at FP16 as well; a pre-existing miss, not an INT8 regression.
One marginal edge-of-frame partial person degrades: score 0.391 -> 0.358 and visible keypoints 2/17 -> 0/17. The box is still emitted; its pose was near-worthless at FP16 too.
detection_sanity.not_measured: This is per-frame detection agreement on 8 frames, not an evaluation-set score. No mAP and no fall-detection F1 was computed for the INT8 weights, and the frozen Subject-4 gate has NOT been re-run on INT8 traces.

conclusions: With the model held constant at YOLO11n and co-resident GPU workloads stopped, Orin NX is the fastest of the edge boards (3.26 ms), followed by Orin Nano (3.69 ms), then RK3588 (51.4 ms) and reCamera 2002 (53.0 ms). That ordering was previously wrong in two ways: Jetson was benchmarked on a heavier model, and contended NX measured below Nano.
Jetson aggregate throughput is essentially flat from 1 to 6 concurrent contexts, so extra contexts split one GPU budget rather than adding capacity.

RKNN INT8 is a free win on both boards: 1.4-1.8x faster with no change in detections-per-frame on held-out real frames. Shipping it still requires re-running the frozen Subject-4 gate, because the temporal profile was frozen against FP16 pose output.

Hailo-8 is the one platform where fixing the model at YOLO11n does not yield a comparable row. The in-house 11n HEF measures 9.01 ms against 6.87 ms for the larger Model Zoo YOLOv8s, because it compiled to 3 contexts rather than 1. The shipped configuration stays on YOLOv8s, which is both faster and larger.

yolo11n_pose.source: compiled in-house, Hailo Dataflow Compiler 3.31.0, 640x640 INT8, 64 GMDCSA-24 calibration frames, raw-head output
yolo11n_pose.why_not: Slower than the s-size Model Zoo build it would replace, and the runtime's post-processing is written against the Model Zoo output layout, not this raw head. No pipeline figure was measured.

yolov8s_pose.source: Hailo Model Zoo v2.15 pre-compiled hailo8 HEF

hailo_int8.finding: The n-size build is 4.3x slower than the larger s-size build on the same accelerator: 9.01 ms vs 6.87 ms. hailortcli parse-hef attributes it to allocation - 11n compiled to 3 contexts, so weights are swapped once per inference, while the Model Zoo s build is single context with resident weights. The compiler had already flagged this: 100% control utilisation on cluster_2 at 16.6% total compute. The number therefore describes this HEF's allocation, not the ceiling for 11n on Hailo-8, and holding the model constant at n does not make Hailo comparable to the other boards the way it does for Jetson and RK.

root_cause.diagnosis: control-resource bound at compile time, not compute bound
root_cause.compile_config: bare compile: the only model script line was the input normalization. No performance_param, no resources_param — allocator ran at its default effort. The Model Zoo yolov8s_pose it is compared against ships with a tuned model script, so this is a tuned build against an untuned one.
root_cause.saturated_clusters: cluster_4 in context 0; cluster_2 and cluster_7 in context 1; cluster_2 in context 2 — all at 100% control while compute on the same context sits at 30-60%.
root_cause.why_nano_hits_this: Control budget is consumed per layer and per output stream, independent of how much arithmetic each layer does. A nano model has no fewer layers than an s model (YOLO11's C3k2/C2PSA branches are more fragmented), and the raw-head export adds 9 separate output streams.

batch_sweep.note: Latency is per batch, not per frame.
batch_sweep.finding: Batching confirms the context-switch diagnosis and does not fix it. The n build recovers 2.15x (92.2 -> 198.3 FPS) as the per-batch switch cost is amortised, but even at batch 16 it reaches only half of what the s build does at batch 1. The s build is flat across batch sizes (393.9 -> 393.8), which is what a single-context network with resident weights looks like. The residual gap is the multi-context split itself, so it has to be fixed at compile time.

remediation: Recompile with performance_param(compiler_optimization_level=max) and a relaxed resources_param ceiling, so the allocator searches harder for a 1- or 2-context fit. Context 2 holds only 16.6% compute and looks mergeable. Costs compile time, no code change. Exact parameter names to be checked against the installed DFC.
Concatenate the 9 raw heads into 3 (one per scale) to cut output-stream and control pressure. Requires changing the ONNX end nodes and the host decoder.
Raise batch size: throughput only, and it caps out at half the s build.
